characters.name: Ilse Vane
characters.arc: protagonist — wants to keep her farm profitable and safe —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 7, Ilse refuses the Baron’s foreman’s offer of payment to remove the waystones, choosing integrity over immediate security.

characters.name: Uncle Eamon
characters.arc: deceased — left the road as a burden —  — — Active Arc: His ledger entries in Chapter 4 reveal he did not just maintain the road; he actively turned away those who sought to stop the travelers’ progress.
characters.voice: recorded in ledger as stoic, silent

characters.name: Baron Kaelen’s Foreman, Torvin
characters.arc: antagonist — wants the stones for his lord’s new hall —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 6, Torvin personally dismantles a waystone at dawn, testing Ilse’s resolve without waiting for her permission.

characters.name: The Traveler, Jaren
characters.arc: catalyst — seeks passage north despite the danger —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 9, Jaren reveals the nature of the "thing" following them, driving Ilse to understand the true cost of the road.

characters.name: Young Elara
characters.arc: innocent — wants to see the sea —  — — Active Arc: In Chapter 8, Elara’s illness forces Ilse to make a medical decision that violates the road’s quarantine rules.

settings.name: Harrow’s End Farm
settings.description: a smallholding of stubborn earth and wind-bent wheat, smelling of damp soil and woodsmoke.

settings.name: The Pilgrim’s Road
settings.description: a cracked stone path winding through hollows, marked by standing stones that hum with cold air.

settings.name: Uncle Eamon’s Cottage
settings.description: a low stone hut near the road’s start, filled with dust and the smell of dried herbs and old paper.

settings.name: The Baron’s Keep
settings.description: a distant silhouette on the hill, cold and imposing, smelling of iron and burnt coal.

settings.name: The Northern Shore
settings.description: a desolate coastline visible only in legend, where the road ends in salt and silence.

plot_points.description: Ilse receives the deed to the road, assuming it is worthless land.
Ilse finds Uncle Eamon’s ledger, noting dates of travelers who never returned.
(inciting incident, ch04) A bruised traveler asks the way, breaking the seven-year silence.
(rising action, ch06) Torvin begins removing waystones; Ilse confronts him, realizing the road’s protection is failing.
Elara falls ill; Ilse must choose between the road’s sanctity and her daughter’s life.
Jaren reveals the "thing" is not a monster, but a consequence of the road’s neglect.
Ilse stands at the final waystone, blocking the Baron’s men and the advancing shadow.
The road holds, but Ilse loses her home to the Baron’s claim.
(epilogue, ch18) The road continues, empty but intact, carrying the memory of those who walked it.

themes: the persistence of memory in silence.
voice: Third-person limited, past tense, measured and austere, rendering landscape as moral geography with aphoristic precision.
